key_insight: Inertia, pitching-axis placement, and reduced frequency jointly control actuator torque phasing in a semi-passive oscillating hydrofoil, strongly shifting mechanical efficiency from hydrodynamic efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The results provide design guidance for hydrokinetic energy harvesters, indicating where to place the pitching axis and how to tune frequency and foil mass to maximize actuator-level power recovery.
method: Experimental characterization of semi-passive oscillating hydrofoils
Varied foil mass ratio, pitching-axis location, and reduced frequency
Used torque-loop analysis and PIV to interpret fluid-structure synchronization
evidence_signal: Experiments identified an optimal reduced frequency range of 0.125-0.16 with quarter-chord to one-third-chord pitching axes and mass ratios of about 0.5-2.0, reaching 33.96% peak mechanical efficiency.
watch_item: Mechanical efficiency can differ from hydrodynamic efficiency by about 38.16%, so design decisions should be based on actuator-level metrics rather than flow-only performance.
paper_title: Inertial effects on the mechanical efficiency of a semi-passive oscillating hydrofoil energy harvester
